events.title: Phone Bank for Chris Bennett
events.description:
Phone Bank for Chris Bennett
CSF DSA endorsed Chris Bennett for Congress (CA-03), and we're phone banking every Wednesday through the June 2 primary to help send him to Washington.
When: Wednesdays, 6–8 PM Pacific Where: Zoom (link sent to your email after you RSVP)
Upcoming sessions:

Wednesday, May 13
Wednesday, May 20
Wednesday, May 27

What to expect
We start with a quick hello, a short chapter update, and a five-minute orientation to the phone banking tool. Then we mute up on Zoom and start calling. Your browser makes the calls, the script is built in, and there's always someone in the room if you have questions.
No experience needed. New volunteers welcome.
What to bring
A laptop or desktop with a working mic, a quiet spot, and a glass of something to drink. If you'd rather call from your phone, you can — just step out of Zoom while you dial and hop back in between calls.
About Chris
Chris Bennett is a DSA member running a grassroots campaign for Medicare for All, a federal jobs guarantee, ending the Iran war and all forever wars, and getting money out of politics. He takes no corporate or AIPAC money. Learn more at bennettforca.com.
RSVP below — we'll send the Zoom link to your email.

events.title: Chapter Meeting
events.description:
When: Sunday, June 14, 2026 at 2:30 PM
Where: Community Room,BriarPatch Food Co-op2505 Bell Rd, Auburn, CA  95603, United States
Format: In-person with hybrid Zoom option
This isn't going to be a standard chapter meeting. Instead of working through a standing agenda, we want to use this time to step back as a chapter and talk together about where CSF DSA is headed.
The chapter has taken on a lot over the past year — endorsing in CA-03, building out a Placerville branch, organizing across four counties. That growth has surfaced real questions about how we sustain the work, who carries it, and what we want to build next.
A few things we'll be putting on the table:

A shared vision for CSF DSA over the next year
How to structure officer roles so they're sustainable
Leadership going into our July/August elections — both co-chairs are likely stepping down, and we want this conversation to include the whole chapter, not just the Steering Committee

Every member should come if they can. Newer members especially — your sense of what brought you in and what you want the chapter to be is exactly what we need in the room.

events.title: Solidarity.tech Training + Phone Bank
events.description:
🗓️ Wednesday, July 16 · 6:00 PM 💻 Zoom (link sent to RSVPs)
Join us for a casual working session on Solidarity.tech, our chapter's organizing platform — part training, part phone bank for our growing Auburn, Roseville, and Placerville branches.
We'll start with a tour of the platform: drafting, scheduling, and sending emails; creating events and event pages; sending and responding to SMS pipes; and the basics of finding contacts, logging calls, and navigating the dashboard. New or just rusty? No experience needed — come as you are.
Once we're warmed up, we'll put it to use and make some calls to help plug interested folks into the new branches. Since we're meeting on Zoom, you'll want access to a computer, your phone, and a stable internet connection.
Please RSVP so we can get you a Solidarity.tech account set up ahead of time and make sure you're ready to go when we start.

events.title: Solidarity Tech Training: Chapter Comms Platform Onboarding
events.description:
Solidarity Tech is the platform CSF DSA uses to manage our contact list and reach members by email, text, and phone. This one-hour session, led by Harry, walks through how it works so any member can use it for chapter, branch, or working group organizing.
We'll cover:

Navigating the contact list: filtering and sorting by branch, county, tags, and activity
Looking up a member and checking membership status and dues standing
Creating events and tracking RSVPs
Sending emails and SMS messages to a list
Setting up and running a phone bank (time permitting)

Who this is for: Branch and working group leads, anyone who sends chapter communications, and any member who wants to help with outreach. No prior experience needed.
Please RSVP early. This is a hands-on session, so we'll set up a Solidarity Tech account for you before we meet. RSVPing a few days ahead gives us time to get your access in place. If you already have an account, you're all set — just RSVP and show up. Your Zoom link will be sent to you after you RSVP.
Bring: A laptop and your Solidarity Tech login.

events.title: [Hybrid] GV/NC Branch Meeting
events.description:
GV/NC Branch Meeting — Monthly
First Thursday of each month | 6:00–8:00 PM Madelyn Helling Library (Gene Albaugh Community Room) 980 Helling Way, Nevada City, CA 95959
Join us for the monthly Grass Valley / Nevada City branch meeting of the Central Sierra Foothills DSA. Socializing from 6:00–6:30, then working groups break out from 6:30–7:30, followed by presentations and updates from 7:30–8:00.
Each meeting covers updates from our working groups — Membership Outreach, Political Education, and the Electoral Working Group — along with chapter business and planning for upcoming actions and events.
New to DSA? This is a great first meeting to attend. Show up, say hi, and see what we're about.
A few members have been getting an informal socialist choir going before meetings — bring an instrument or your voice if you're interested (please be mindful of library noise policies).
Zoom available for remote attendance — we're still dialing in the hybrid setup, so in-person is preferred.
Questions? Reach us at foothillsdsa@gmail.com or on Slack.
